Kitchen

The Kitchen

Drink first

Many people worry that water retention means looking puffy or bloated.

However, because creatine utilizes intracellular hydration, the water is stored inside the muscle cells rather than under the skin. This gives muscles a noticeably fuller, harder appearance rather than a soft, watery look.

The average adult loses 300 to 400 mL of water every single night just through breathing and sweating while asleep.

About 10 to 14 ounces.

When creatine forces water inside your muscle cells, the cells physically expand.

This cellular swelling acts as a biological trigger that tells your body it is in a nutrient-rich environment. This cell volumization sets an environment for protein synthesis and muscle repair to occur. Essentially, the water absorption itself tells your body to build and repair muscle faster.
